subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does adding white to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding white to a colour produces a tint (a lighter version), while adding black produces a shade.

options: The dream world and the unconscious mind
questions.explain: Surrealism drew on dreams and the unconscious to create strange, irrational imagery.

questions.q: Which group are considered warm colours?
questions.explain: Reds, oranges and yellows are warm colours, while blues, greens and violets are cool.

questions.q: A 'hue' refers to which property of colour?
options: The pure colour itself, such as red or blue
questions.explain: Hue is the name of the pure colour, such as red, yellow or blue, before tints or shades are added.

questions.q: The rule of thirds suggests you place key features where?
options: Along lines that divide the image into thirds or at their intersections
In the exact centre of the image
Around the edges of the frame
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the picture into a 3x3 grid and places focal points on the lines or intersections.

options: The appearance of texture created on a flat surface
Texture you can physically feel on the surface
questions.explain: Visual texture is the illusion of texture on a flat surface, whereas actual texture can be touched.

questions.q: What does 'tone' refer to in the formal elements?
options: The lightness or darkness of an area
questions.explain: Tone describes how light or dark an area is, helping to create the illusion of form.

questions.q: Which assessment objective involves responding to the work of other artists?
options: Developing ideas through investigation of sources
questions.explain: Developing ideas requires investigating sources, including the work of relevant artists and cultures.

questions.q: What is the shading technique of drawing closely spaced parallel lines called?
questions.explain: Hatching builds tone using sets of parallel lines; crossing a second set over them is cross-hatching.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'annotation' in a sketchbook?
options: To fill empty space with decoration
To explain your thinking, choices and development in words
To list the cost of materials
questions.explain: Annotation uses written notes to explain your ideas, decisions and how your work is developing.

questions.q: When analysing an artwork, which is the best opening focus?
options: How long it took to frame
What you can see and how the formal elements are used
questions.explain: Good analysis starts by describing what you see and how line, colour, tone and composition are used.

options: The arrangement of elements within an artwork
The size of the canvas only
questions.explain: Composition is how the visual elements are arranged and organised within the picture area.
